lms: Canvas (Instructure) — university-wide LMS across all IU campuses
ai_guidance: IU provides generative AI teaching guidance through Teaching.IU and UITS's 'AI at IU' hub. Faculty are urged to include a clear GenAI syllabus statement; public tools like ChatGPT and Claude are not approved for institutional data, and IU approves no AI-detection tools for student work.
enterprise_ai_tools: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat (free for all IU users 18+, enterprise data protection; IU's preferred GenAI service); paid Microsoft 365 Copilot integration also available.
notable: GenAI 101, IU's free generative AI course, was opened to anyone worldwide. IU explicitly approves no GenAI-detection tools, citing accuracy and bias concerns.
syllabus_policy_approach: Instructor and school discretion — no campus-wide rule; faculty set course-level GenAI policies in the syllabus.

sources.title: Policies and Guidance: Generative AI — Teaching.IU

lms: ICON (Iowa Courses Online), powered by Canvas
ai_guidance: The Office of Teaching, Learning, and Technology and the Center for Teaching jointly maintain 'AI Tools and Teaching' guidance with sample syllabus policy language; the Provost's 'AI in the Classroom' page emphasizes helping students use AI effectively and ethically.
enterprise_ai_tools: Microsoft Copilot Chat (free with enterprise data protection; the university's preferred GenAI tool) and Microsoft 365 Copilot; Cogniti (AI teaching-agent platform) being integrated into ICON.
notable: Piloted Khanmigo Teacher Tools (AI teaching assistant in Canvas) in spring 2025; runs an 'AI in the Classroom' Community of Practice.
syllabus_policy_approach: Instructor discretion — campus provides sample syllabus language for a range of stances (prohibit, conditional, encourage).

sources.title: AI Tools and Teaching — OTLT, University of Iowa
AI in the Classroom — Office of the Provost

ai_guidance: UMD's 'Guidelines for the Use of Generative AI Tools' (ai.umd.edu) set best practices for ethical, transparent use with disclosure/attribution expectations; the Teaching & Learning Transformation Center provides AI-in-teaching resources, sample syllabus language, and an AI Literacy module for ELMS-Canvas courses.
enterprise_ai_tools: Google Gemini (in UMD's Google Workspace) and Microsoft Copilot (in M365), both with enterprise data protections; Canvas-integrated 'Digital Study Assistant' bots.
notable: Launched the Artificial Intelligence Interdisciplinary Institute at Maryland (AIM) in April 2024, directed by Hal Daumé III, spanning all 12 colleges and coordinating new AI majors/minors.
syllabus_policy_approach: Instructor discretion — whether and how GenAI may be used is explicitly at the course instructor's discretion, with TLTC sample syllabus language.

lms: Canvas (Instructure) — the University of Nebraska system's shared LMS
ai_guidance: UNL's Center for Transformative Teaching maintains 'Teaching and Generative Artificial Intelligence' resources covering course policy development, AI-resistant assessment design, and an AI Exchange of faculty practices; a system-wide AI Taskforce provides overarching guidance.
enterprise_ai_tools: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat (free for all NU students/faculty/staff), Copilot Studio, Zoom AI Companion; ChatGPT Edu pilot via OpenAI collaboration (up to 200 UNL faculty/staff licenses under the OpenAI Impact Program).
notable: The NU system is piloting ChatGPT Edu across campuses in collaboration with OpenAI and runs a system-wide University of Nebraska AI Institute (ai.nebraska.edu).
syllabus_policy_approach: Instructor discretion — CTT guidance helps faculty develop their own course AI policies; no single campus-wide classroom rule.

sources.title: Teaching and Generative AI — CTT, UNL

ai_guidance: Northwestern's provost-level AI and Education Advisory Committee and ai.northwestern.edu guide GenAI use in courses with a Closed/Conditional/Open framework: instructors decide whether GenAI is prohibited, permitted when authorized, or encouraged.
enterprise_ai_tools: Microsoft Copilot Chat free for all (enterprise data protection; includes OpenAI GPT and Anthropic Claude models); GitHub Copilot for coding; Google Gemini and Zoom AI Companion under review.
notable: Generative AI 101, a cohort-based faculty development program run with the Provost's office; Northwestern IT built its own AI-enabled Canvas chatbot (featured in EDUCAUSE Review).
syllabus_policy_approach: Instructor discretion within a recommended Closed/Conditional/Open course framework; the Registrar provides an optional GenAI syllabus statement.
